title: Balance for Better Living – Awareness Session on Stress & Nutrition
body:

title: Caritas Hospital Leads Community-Driven Palliative Care Strengthening Initiative at Kaduthuruthy
body:
The 'Palliative Care Unit Strengthening Program,' jointly organized by the Health Commission of the Kottayam Archeparchy, Caritas Hospital, and the Kaduthuruthy Forane, was successfully held on March 1st at Kaduthuruthy Church. The event was inaugurated by Rev. Dr. Binu Kunnath, Director and CEO of Caritas Hospital, while Rev. Fr Johnson Neelanirappel, Vicar of Kaduthuruthy Church, presided over the function.

Aimed at empowering palliative units with modern facilities, the project distributed essential medical equipment including hospital beds, mattresses, wheelchairs, walkers, oxygen concentrators, and sugar-BP monitoring machines. In addition to the distribution, an awareness seminar and volunteer training session were led by Dr. Krishnapriya V from the Palliative Medicine Department of Caritas Hospital.

This initiative was made possible through the full cooperation of the parishes of Kaduthuruthy, Eravimangalam, Karippadam, Memmury, Kothanalloor, Thottara, Arunootimangalam, Poozhikkol, Neezhoor, and Kallara, program also attended by Senior Specialist Dr. Jose Jom and other Forane priests.

title: Caritas LIFE Initiative Hosts Basic Life Support and Emergency Response Training Session
body:
Caritas Hospital & Institute of Health Sciences, under the Caritas LIFE (Caritas Social Responsibility) initiative, successfully conducted a training session on Basic Life Support (BLS) and Common Emergencies.

The session was led by Dr. Vivek R, HOD & Senior Consultant – Emergency Physician, along with Team Emergency Medicine, Caritas Hospital. They provided expert, hands-on guidance on life-saving techniques and how to respond effectively during medical emergencies.

Held at the Neerikkad SNDP Auditorium in collaboration with Thejas Purusha Swayamsahaya Sangham, the program witnessed enthusiastic participation and meaningful interactions. This initiative reinforces our ongoing commitment to empowering the community with the skills and confidence needed to save lives.

title: Building Life-Saving Skills: BLS & Common Emergencies Training Initiative

title: 'Cancer Shield’ Project Launched
body:
As part of V-Guard Industries Limited’s CSR initiative, in association with Caritas Hospital, the ‘Cancer Shield’ health protection project has been launched for women police officers in Kottayam district and the family members of police personnel. Implemented in collaboration with Caritas Hospital, the project offers free mammogram and ultrasound scan examinations. The inauguration and flag-off ceremony of the project was performed by the Honorable Kerala Minister for Ports, Cooperation and Devaswom, Shri. V. N. Vasavan.

V-Guard has introduced this project as a gesture of gratitude for the unparalleled and dedicated service of the Kerala Police. Through the Cancer Shield project, the main focus is on the importance of timely health screenings and adopting healthy habits that can help reduce the risk of disease. Emphasizing that early diagnosis is one of the most important factors in preventing loss of life, V-Guard Foundation Director Dr. Reena Mithun Chittilappilly said so.

The screenings will be conducted from February 2 to March 7. The camps will be organized at various locations across Kottayam district using a specially equipped mobile mammogram unit of Caritas Hospital and Institute of Health Sciences.

The event was attended by Kottayam District Collector Shri. Chetan Kumar Meena, IAS, District Police Chief Shri. Shahul Hameed A, IPS, and Director & CEO of Caritas Hospital, Rev. Dr. Binu Kunnath.

This health protection project is being implemented with the participation of the Kerala Police Senior Officers Association, Kerala Police Officers Association, and Kerala Police Association.

title: Caritas Hospital Hosts “Pratheeksha” to Inspire Hope and Raise Awareness on Breast Cancer
body:
As part of Breast Cancer Awareness Month, Caritas Hospital organized a special event called "Pratheeksha" at the Diamond Jubilee Hall. The program, held on October 10th at 3:30 PM, featured Dr. Boban Thomas, Senior Consultant in Medical Oncology, delivering the welcome address. Rev. Dr. Binu Kunnath, Director of Caritas Hospital, presided over the function, with actress and TV anchor Jewel Mary as the chief guest. Jewel Mary, a thyroid cancer survivor, shared her personal experiences and survival memories with the audience. Sub Inspector Shanthi K Balu of the Narcotics Cell offered felicitations, while Prof. Dr. Jose Tom, Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology, expressed gratitude.

The event also included the unveiling of a special package for teachers called "Pink Teachers." Additionally, the hospital celebrated the completion of 500 free mammogram screening tests within a year through its Mobile Mammogram Unit.

Rev. Dr. Binu Kunnath, Director & CEO of Caritas Hospital, stated that the gathering was a testament to the hope and resilience of cancer survivors and those fighting the disease. During the event, Federal Bank Foundation was honored for its support in providing financial assistance to economically disadvantaged cancer patients.

title: Uniting for Heart Health: Caritas Hospital and Decathlon Host World Heart Day Marathon
body:
Upholding the message of World Heart Day, Caritas Hospital and Decathlon jointly organized a marathon. The marathon, which started at 6:30 AM from Caritas Matha Hospital, was flagged off by Ettumanoor CI Anzil A.S.

Rev. Dr. Binu Kunnath (Director & CEO, Caritas Hospital), Rev. Fr. Joice Nandikunnel (Joint Director, Operations) and Rev. Fr. Jismon Madathil (Joint Director, Media & Relations), and Dr. Deepak Davidson (Chief Interventional Cardiologist & Senior Consultant, Caritas Heart Institute) were present on the occasion. The marathon, which began from Caritas Matha Hospital, passed through Caritas Roundabout (Pattithanam) and Ettumanoor, and concluded back at Caritas Matha Hospital around 8:00 AM.

The participants were categorized into three main groups – employees, students, and the general public – with separate competitions organized for men and women. During the prize distribution ceremony held after the marathon, winners were awarded cash prizes, while all participants received certificates and medals.

title: A Mobile Lifeline for Breast Health,Caritas Hospital Takes Breast Cancer Screening to the Next Level
body:
n our unwavering commitment to providing accessible and high-quality healthcare, Caritas Hospital is proud to introduce our advanced mobile mammogram bus. This innovative initiative is designed to bring breast cancer screening directly to your community, making it easier than ever to prioritize your health.

Breast cancer is a significant health concern, but early detection through regular mammograms can significantly improve outcomes. However, geographic and logistical barriers can often hinder access to timely screenings. Our mobile mammogram bus aims to bridge this gap by offering convenient and accessible screening services.

The Benefits of Our Mobile Mammogram Bus
  • Convenience: No need to travel to the hospital. Our mobile unit comes to you.
  • Accessibility: We serve diverse communities, reaching even the most remote areas.
  • Comfort: Experience a comfortable and efficient screening process.
  • Expertise: Our skilled technicians provide accurate and reliable screenings.

By utilising our mobile mammogram bus, you're taking a proactive step towards safeguarding your health. Schedule your screening today and empower yourself with early detection.

title: Caritas Hospital Introduced South Kerala’s First Drone-Based Medical Deliveries Unit
body:
Kottayam: Caritas Hospital, a leading healthcare provider in Kerala, has taken a significant step towards revolutionising healthcare by successfully introducing South Kerala's first Drone-Based Medical Deliveries at Caritas Hospital by partnering with Skye Air Mobility, a pioneering drone technology firm. This groundbreaking collaboration aims to enhance healthcare accessibility and efficiency in Kottayam and surrounding areas through the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) for the transportation of essential medical supplies and diagnostic samples.

The innovative drone delivery system will connect Caritas Hospital with various other healthcare facilities within the Caritas network and remote areas in the region. The drone can carry payloads of up to 5 kilograms over a distance of 15 kilometres. By leveraging drones, the hospital aims to significantly reduce delivery times from hours to just 5-7 minutes, ensuring critical medical supplies reach their destinations swiftly and efficiently.

During the inaugural ceremony, attended by local dignitaries and healthcare professionals, the first drone flight successfully transported a package of vital medicines from Caritas Hospital to Caritas Family Hospital and Caritas KMM located 10-15 kilometres away. This marked a historic milestone in the adoption of drone technology for healthcare purposes in Kottayam.

Dr. Binu Kunnath, Director of Caritas Hospital, expressed enthusiasm about the collaboration, stating, "We're excited to work with Skye Air Mobility on this project. Drones are a game-changer for healthcare in Kottayam, helping us reach patients in remote areas much faster and more reliably. Whether it's delivering medicine, transporting lab samples, or providing medical equipment, these drones will improve care in our community. We look forward to seeing the positive impact this will have on healthcare in our region."

The drone delivery program is expected to have a profound impact on healthcare in Kottayam. It will enable the hospital to provide faster and more efficient services, especially in emergency situations. Additionally, the use of drones will help reduce the carbon footprint associated with traditional transportation methods, contributing to a more sustainable healthcare system.

This partnership between Caritas Hospital and Skye Air Mobility represents a significant step forward in the adoption of innovative technologies in healthcare. By embracing drones for medical deliveries, the hospital is demonstrating its commitment to improving patient care and enhancing healthcare accessibility in Kottayam and beyond.

body: Caritas Hospital Partners with Federal Bank's Sanjeevani Scheme to Aid Cancer Patients

title: Caritas Hospital Wins Kerala State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB) Award
body:
Caritas Hospital has been awarded the prestigious accolade for Best Environmental Activities by the Kerala State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB) for the year 2024. The event, which took place as part of World Environment Day celebrations, was formally inaugurated by Chief Minister Shri Pinarayi Vijayan. Among the dignitaries present were Shri M.B. Rajesh MLA, Shri M. Vincent MLA, Shri Kadakampally Surendran MLA, and Shri V.K. Prashanth MLA.

The awards, a government tradition since 1989, recognize outstanding pollution control management practices across various sectors. Caritas Hospital's notable achievements in pollution control and environmental conservation made it the standout winner. Over the past nine years, Caritas has consistently won the awards, demonstrating a commitment to environmental stewardship.

Dr. Fr. Binu Kunnathu, Director of Caritas Hospital, expressed gratitude for the recognition and emphasized the hospital's dedication to integrating nature into its operations. He stressed the importance of this achievement as a testament to their efforts and pledged to continue their environmental initiatives.

Moreover, during the event, the official publication of environmental news was done by the Trivandrum Corporation Mayor Smt. Arya Rajendran. The Integrated Web Portal of the Board, was launched by Dr. V. Venugopal IAS, Chief Secretary. Smt. Sharada G. Muralidharan, IAS, Additional Chief Secretary for Local Self-Government and Resources and Additional Chief Secretary for Water-Air Quality, officated the Diary Launch.

title: World Environment Day
body:
Caritas Hospital & Institute of Health Sciences hosted a program to mark World Environment Day! The theme this year was Land Restoration, Desertification and Drought Resilience. Rev. Dr. Binu Kunnath, Director of Caritas Hospital, delivered an inspirational message.

Rev. Dr. Bressan Ozhungalil, Director of Pastoral Care, welcomed the audience with an opening speech. Sreesankar TP, District Coordinator of the Malinyamuktam Navakeralam project, led an informative session on the chosen theme. The program concluded with a vote of thanks delivered by Fr. Abey Alex Vadakkekara, Joint Director of the Pastoral Care Department.

title: World Blood Donor Day at Caritas Hospital
body: In honor of World Blood Donor Day, Caritas Hospital and Caritas Nursing College joined forces to host a blood donation camp! The program was inaugurated by the esteemed Rev. Fr. Dr. Brasson Ozhungalil, Director of Pastoral Care, who delivered an inspiring message about the significance of blood donation. Caritas Hospital and Caritas Nursing College express heartfelt gratitude to all the blood donors and the dedicated volunteers who made this blood donation camp a resounding success.

title: Palliative Care Training 2024
body:
Caritas Hospital in collaboration with Caritas College of Nursing, conducted Palliative Care Training 2024 on May 31 from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m. at Diamond Jubilee Hall to give special palliative care training to selected people. It is crucial to provide tailored medical care for people living with illnesses.

Rev. Dr. Binu Kunnath, Director, acknowledged the vital role of Inauguration of program, Guest Rtd. Prof. Dr. Saramma Varghese (Hod and Senior Consultant - Pain and PalliativeMedicine), Ms. Sheela Rani ( National Florence Nightingale Award Winner 2022) and Mr. Zacharias Njavally ( Founder Swaruma Charitable Society). Dr. Sharon Raj Eliza, Consultant - Community Medicine and Dr. Manu John - Senior Consultant- Palliative Oncology took class on Palliative Care model and Hydration in Palliative Care and felicitation by Rev. Fr Jismon Madathil, Joint Director Media and Relations.

title: Caritas Hospital Celebrates Educational Milestones of Staff Children
body:
Caritas Hospital, in collaboration with Caritas Staff Welfare, organized a special program to celebrate the educational achievements of children of hospital staff entering their first classes in schools and students achieving outstanding results in their Class 12 exams.

Held at the Nursing College Auditorium, the program was presided over by Rev. Fr. Dr. Binu Kunnath, Director of Caritas Hospital, and inaugurated by Rev. Fr. Dr. Thomas Puthiyakunnel.

Nearly 500 children entering nursery or first grade this year were welcomed into the world of learning. They received gift bags containing essential school supplies like water bottles and colorful books to kickstart their educational journeys.The event highlights Caritas Hospital's dedication to the community, extending beyond healthcare services to encompass the educational aspirations of its staff's families.

Approximately 20 students who aced their Class 12 exams were felicitated at the ceremony. Caritas Hospital acknowledges these high achievers as future leaders with immense potential.

In his address, Rev. Fr. Dr. Binu Kunnath emphasized the children's role in shaping the future of Caritas Hospital and the nation. He expressed his hope that they would not only excel academically but also inspire others through their achievements.

With a workforce of nearly 3,000 employees, Caritas Hospital has a tradition of recognizing its staff's dedication. This event marks their five-year commitment to valuing their employees and their families, who are the foundation of their service mission.

The program was filled with joy and celebration, with vibrant cultural performances from children.

title: Caritas Hospital Kottayam distribution of Caritas Privilege Card
body:
As part of the Padamugham Forane centenary celebrations, the Caritas Privilege Card distribution and the formation of a health community involving Caritas Hospital doctors and nurses were held. Kottayam Diocese Bishop Mar Mathew Moolakkatt inaugurated the ceremony. Idukki Diocese Bishop Mar John Nellikunnel and Vijayapuram Diocese Auxiliary Bishop Rt. Rev. Justin Alexander Madathiparambil were also present at the ceremony.

Caritas Hospital has designed this project as a tribute to Padamugham Forane, which has made invaluable contributions to the Knanaya Catholic Church. Through this, Forane members with privilege cards will be able to avail treatment and other benefits at a 10% discount.

title: Kenyan Priest Finds Hope and Healing at Caritas Hospital
body:
Fr. John Baptist's story is a powerful testament to the unwavering commitment of Caritas Hospital to healing even in the face of immense challenges. Hailing from Kenya, Fr. Baptist was diagnosed with a complex brain tumor, leaving him with a daunting path to recovery.

Seeking hope and a fresh start, Fr. Baptist entrusted his care to the Caritas Hospital team. The hospital, known for its unparalleled expertise and compassionate approach, provided Fr. Baptist with the dedicated care he needed. This dedication, coupled with the team's extensive knowledge, has led to what Caritas Hospital describes as "miraculous outcomes."

Fr. Baptist's case highlights the extraordinary efforts undertaken daily by the Caritas Hospital staff. The hospital expresses its deep humility for Fr. Baptist's unwavering trust in their abilities and is profoundly inspired by his remarkable recovery.

title: Helping Hands for Cancer Patients
body:
Caritas Hospital and SDM Cancer Relief Fund have come together to provide financial assistance to 40 cancer patients. SDM Cancer Relief Fund representative, Dr. Jose Tom (HOD, Oncology - Caritas Hospital), Fr. Jinu Kavil (Caritas Joint Director), Dr. Bobby (Medical Director - Caritas Hospital), and Dr. Manu John (Palliative Oncologist) were present at the function where financial assistance of Rs 10 lakh was distributed to 40 cancer patients.

Caritas Hospital Director, Fr. Binu Kunath, expressed Caritas' pride in being part of this impactful initiative. Though it might seem like a modest contribution, it brings assistance to roughly 40 families. Caritas, true to its motto of "Kenotic Love," will resolutely fulfill its societal commitment through various acts of compassion.
